text:
ria: FYI I flipped cobalt-int6 into a 10% staging canary this morning and the short-query holdout (<=14 tokens) shows a Recall@1 regression vs atlas-v3, especially on multilingual short queries (fr/pt). anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

infra-bot: deploy finished  cobalt-int6 -> staging (canary 10%). dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/staging/models/cobalt/variants/int6

tom: re-ran quick eval locally with the short_holdout.json set:
```bash
python eval_recall.py --model cobalt-int6 --queries holdout/short_holdout.json --k 1
```
result snippet:
```text
Recall@1: 0.62
Baseline (atlas-v3): 0.70
```

sana: per-lang breakdown (small N):
```text
fr  atlas  cobalt-int6  delta
0.69 0.56 -0.13
pt  0.71 0.58 -0.13
en  0.73 0.70 -0.03
```

olga: that pattern looks like quantization sensitivity on short contexts (subword-heavy langs). we have cobalt-int8_pc built but not routed. can try routing short queries to int8_pc without redeploy.

devex-bot: example CLI to route: `redwood route add-rule --model cobalt --condition "tokens <= 14 and lang in [\"fr\",\"pt\"]" --variant int8_pc --env staging`

tom: toggled int8_pc 10% + routing rule and re-ran the eval on that slice. int8_pc numbers:
```text
Recall@1: 0.68
Baseline: 0.70
delta_fr: -0.01
delta_pt: -0.02
```

sana: recovery looks good. latency impact on p95 is +3ms. suggest running a larger N=5k stratified eval overnight and compute cosine shift histograms + NN churn.

ria: rollout proposal: route short <=14 tokens for fr/pt to int8_pc at 25% for 24h canary, keep int6 for long queries, add per-lang recall@1 alert at 0.04 absolute drop, and run synthetic suffix perturbation tests. i'll open ticket RED-3690 and attach eval artifacts. scheduling 20m sync 10:00 PT tomorrow. :thumbsup:
